subject: Provisional capacity bridge & nonstandard overage terms for Voxalyte pilot
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@voxalyte.io>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ramp / short-term mix request

Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re targeting a small public pilot in May and need to lock dedicated capacity for the pilot window (6 weeks). Our workload will spike in short bursts and the H100-type SKUs we tested look ideal for latency, but our cost team will only sign if we can keep overage exposure controlled.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provision a short-term capacity bridge that mixes H100-equivalent and H200-equivalent instances for Q2? We may need H200 (memory) for some batches but H100 for inference-critical routes.
- Can you provisionally hold the reservation (no capacity expiry) while our PO clears? We expect procurement to finish in ~3 weeks.

We’re also asking for a capped overage rate (max $/GPU-hour) for bursts above committed-hours — otherwise the CFO won’t greenlight.

Attached a draft SOW and an outline of the target burst profile.

Appreciate your help — Emma

--
Emma Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Voxalyte
emma@voxalyte.io

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Emma Liu <emma@voxalyte.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ramp / short-term mix request

Emma — thanks for the clear note and the SOW. I’m looping in Lauren (deal desk) and Karthik (sales ops) to scope an internal approval path.

Short answers: we can support mixed-GPU allocations and we commonly do short-term "capacity bridges," but the nonstandard pieces — provisional reservation hold and a hard-capped overage rate — will need exec sign-off. I’ll get pricing/impact from Karthik and propose a conditional approval approach to Lauren and our VP Sales.

Can you confirm: the pilot committed baseline is 10 concurrent units for 6 weeks, with bursts up to 30 concurrent units for 2–4 hour windows? I’ll use that to model cost.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot ramp / short-term mix request

Lauren / Rafael — I ran the numbers on the proposed profile (attached spreadsheet). Key points:

- Baseline: 10 units reserved (6 weeks) 
- Burst windows: up to 30 units for ~3 hours/day on average across pilot week nights — estimated incremental token-hours ~ 4.5k GPU-hours over 6 weeks
- SKU mix: ~60% H100-equivalent inference nodes, 40% H200-equivalent memory nodes during combined allocation
- Cost impact: standalone list pricing would put overage exposure at ~$62k across pilot if un-capped (based on current on-demand H100/H200 blend).

Proposed mitigations to make it signable:
1) Provision a 21-day provisional reservation hold (no capacity release for 21 days) while procurement completes.
2) Offer a capped overage rate at $1.60 / GPU-hour (effective blended cap) for any burst usage above committed-hours during the pilot. This is ~25% below our current on-demand blended price and reduces Voxalyte CFO risk.
3) Apply a short-term 12% pilot discount on committed capacity for the 6-week term (one-off concession).

Financial impact to Redwood (rule of thumb): ~40% hit to margin on those incremental burst-hours if we accept the cap. This is tolerable for a strategic pilot with strong expansion potential, but requires AVP+ signoff per our escalation matrix.

If Lauren/Lauren's approver is comfortable with the cap and 21-day hold, we can present to Vanessa for exec approval.

Karthik
Sales Operations

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot ramp / short-term mix request

Team — I recommend we approve the request with explicit guardrails. Summary for exec: Voxalyte asks for a temporary mixed SKU allocation, a 21-day reservation hold while their PO clears, a blended-capped overage of $1.60/GPU-hour, and a 12% concession on committed-hours for the 6-week pilot.

Conditions I suggest we attach to approval:
- Approved only for a single pilot term (6 weeks). No auto-renew or roll-forward.
- Overage cap applies only to the pilot burst windows described in their SOW; any sustained usage outside the profile falls back to standard overage pricing.
- Voxalyte provides an escalated procurement contact and confirms PO ETA within 10 business days; if we don’t receive the PO or a firm update by day 21 we release the provisional hold.
- We require a signed addendum to the SOW capturing the cap, term, and the rollback clause.

If Vanessa signs off with those conditions, Finance will enter a one-time accounting code for the discounted margin and Sales Ops will track usage daily. Approve?

—Lauren
Head of Deal Desk

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot ramp / short-term mix request

Thanks — reviewed. I approve the temporary concession under the conditions Lauren outlined. Specifics:

- Approve 21-day provisional reservation hold starting on first allocation date; Redwood will not release capacity for that 21-day window.
- Approve blended capped overage at $1.60/GPU-hour for pilot burst windows (per SOW table).
- Approve 12% one-time committed capacity discount for the 6-week term.

Operational notes: Sales Ops to create a usage alert that pings Deal Desk at 75% of the burst forecast; Finance to accept one-time margin variance for the period. No further concessions without VP+ review.

Rafael — move forward with the addendum and DocuSign; confirm procurement contact and PO ETA. Karthik — post the concession to the deal record and enable the provisional hold tag.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
